rows.stem: When 2 mL of sodium hydroxide solution is added to few pieces of granulated zinc in a test tube and then warmed, the reaction that occurs can be written in the form of a balanced chemical equation as :
rows.solution:
Zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide on warming to give sodium zincate and hydrogen gas:

\(\mathrm{2NaOH + Zn \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2}\)

Check: Na 2 = 2; O 2 = 2; H 2 = 2; Zn 1 = 1. The product is hydrogen gas, not water, and sodium zincate is \(\mathrm{Na_2ZnO_2}\).

This is option (B) \(\mathrm{2NaOH + Zn \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2}\).

rows.stem: Select from the following a decomposition reaction in which source of energy for decomposition is light :
rows.solution:
Silver bromide decomposes in sunlight into silver and bromine, so light supplies the energy:

\(\mathrm{2AgBr(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Br_2(g)}\)

(Ferrous sulphate and calcium carbonate decompose on heating, and water is decomposed by electricity.)

This is option (C) \(\mathrm{2AgBr \rightarrow 2Ag + Br_2}\).

rows.subtopic: Physical Properties of Metals and Non-metals
rows.stem: A metal and a non-metal that exists in liquid state at the room temperature are respectively :
rows.solution:
Mercury is the only metal that is a liquid at room temperature, and bromine is the only non-metal that is a liquid at room temperature. Iodine is a solid.

This is option (C) Mercury and Bromine.

rows.stem:
Carbon compounds :

(i) are good conductors of electricity.

(ii) are bad conductors of electricity.

(iii) have strong forces of attraction between their molecules.

(iv) have weak forces of attraction between their molecules.

The correct statements are :
rows.solution:
Carbon compounds are mostly covalent and do not form ions, so they are bad conductors of electricity. The forces of attraction between their molecules are weak, which is why they have low melting and boiling points. So (ii) and (iv) are correct.

This is option (C) (ii) and (iv).

rows.stem:
Consider the following compounds :

\(\mathrm{FeSO_4}\) ; \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\) ; \(\mathrm{CaSO_4}\) ; \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}\)

The compound having maximum number of water of crystallisation in its crystalline form in one molecule is :
rows.solution:
In their crystalline forms the salts are \(\mathrm{FeSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O}\), \(\mathrm{CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O}\), \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O}\) (gypsum) and \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\) (washing soda). Washing soda has the most, ten molecules of water of crystallisation.

This is option (D) \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}\).

rows.stem: Oxides of aluminium and zinc are :
rows.solution:
Aluminium oxide and zinc oxide react with both acids and bases to give salt and water, so they are amphoteric oxides. For example,

\(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 6HCl \rightarrow 2AlCl_3 + 3H_2O}\)

\(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 2NaOH \rightarrow 2NaAlO_2 + H_2O}\)

This is option (C) amphoteric.

rows.stem:
\(\mathrm{MnO_2 + 4HCl \rightarrow MnCl_2 + 2H_2O + Cl_2}\)

The reaction given above is a redox reaction because in this case :

options.label: A
options.text: \(\mathrm{MnO_2}\) is oxidised and HCl is reduced.

options.label: D
options.text: \(\mathrm{MnO_2}\) is reduced and HCl is oxidised.

rows.solution:
\(\mathrm{MnO_2}\) loses oxygen and becomes \(\mathrm{MnCl_2}\), so it is reduced. HCl loses hydrogen and gives chlorine gas, so it is oxidised. One substance is reduced while the other is oxidised, which makes it a redox reaction.

This is option (D) \(\mathrm{MnO_2}\) is reduced and HCl is oxidised.

rows.stem:
Consider the following statements :

(i) The sex of a child is determined by what it inherits from the mother.

(ii) The sex of a child is determined by what it inherits from the father.

(iii) The probability of having a male child is more than that of a female child.

(iv) The sex of a child is determined at the time of fertilisation when male and female gametes fuse to form a zygote.

The correct statements are :
rows.solution:
The mother has XX sex chromosomes, so every egg carries an X. The father has XY, so half his sperms carry X and half carry Y. A child who inherits X from the father is a girl, and one who inherits Y is a boy, so the sex is decided by what is inherited from the father, at fertilisation, when the gametes fuse to form the zygote. The chances of a boy and a girl are equal (50 : 50), so (i) and (iii) are false.

This is option (B) (ii) and (iv).

rows.stem:
Chromosomes :

(i) carry hereditary information from parents to the next generation.

(ii) are thread like structures located inside the nucleus of an animal cell.

(iii) always exist in pairs in human reproductive cells.

(iv) are involved in the process of cell division.

The correct statements are :
rows.solution:
Chromosomes carry the hereditary information (as DNA) from parents to the next generation, so (i) is true. They are copied and shared between the daughter cells, so they take part in cell division, and (iv) is true. Reproductive cells (gametes) carry only one chromosome of each pair, so (iii) is false.

Statement (ii) is the one in doubt. Chromosomes are present in the nucleus of every eukaryotic cell, plant as well as animal, and they are seen as distinct thread-like structures only when the cell is dividing; in a resting nucleus the material is spread out as a chromatin network. The marking scheme does not count (ii) as one of the intended correct statements. Read literally, though, (ii) is a true description of chromosomes in an animal cell, and on that reading the choice "(i), (ii) and (iv)" would be correct.

The marking scheme's answer is option (D) (i) and (iv).

rows.stem: In a nerve cell, the site where the electrical impulse is converted into a chemical signal is known as :
rows.solution:
A nerve impulse travels as an electrical signal from the dendrite, through the cell body, along the axon to its end. At the nerve ending the electrical impulse sets off the release of chemicals, which cross the gap and start an impulse in the next cell. Where a nerve ending meets a muscle cell, this junction is the neuromuscular junction, and there the electrical impulse is converted into a chemical signal that makes the muscle contract.

Strictly, the conversion takes place at the end of the axon, at any synapse, so a student could defend the choice "Axon". The marking scheme takes the junction as the site.

The marking scheme's answer is option (C) Neuromuscular junction.

rows.stem:
A stomata closes when :

(i) it needs carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.

(ii) it does not need carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.

(iii) water flows out of the guard cells.

(iv) water flows into the guard cells.

The correct reason(s) in this process is/are :
rows.solution:
The guard cells close the stomatal pore when the leaf does not need carbon dioxide for photosynthesis (and to cut water loss). The pore closes when water flows out of the guard cells and they shrink; when water flows in, they swell and the pore opens. So (ii) and (iii) are correct.

This is option (C) (ii) and (iii).

rows.stem: At what distance from a convex lens should an object be placed to get an image of the same size as that of the object on a screen ?

options.label: A
options.text: Beyond twice the focal length of the lens.

options.label: B
options.text: At the principal focus of the lens.

options.label: C
options.text: At twice the focal length of the lens.

options.label: D
options.text: Between the optical centre of the lens and its principal focus.

rows.solution:
For a convex lens, an object placed at \(2F_1\) (twice the focal length) gives a real, inverted image at \(2F_2\), of the same size as the object, which can be taken on a screen. An object beyond \(2F_1\) gives a smaller image, and one between the optical centre and the focus gives a virtual image that cannot be taken on a screen.

This is option (C) At twice the focal length of the lens.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: The lens system of human eye forms an image on a light sensitive screen, which is called as :
rows.solution:
The eye lens forms a real, inverted image on the retina, the light-sensitive screen at the back of the eye. Its cells send signals through the optic nerve to the brain.

This is option (D) Retina.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem: The pattern of the magnetic field produced inside a current carrying solenoid is :

options.label: A
options.text: Diagram (A) as printed - a magnetic field-line pattern; see the attached figure.

options.label: B
options.text: Diagram (B) as printed - a magnetic field-line pattern; see the attached figure.

options.label: C
options.text: Diagram (C) as printed - a magnetic field-line pattern; see the attached figure.

options.label: D
options.text: Diagram (D) as printed - a magnetic field-line pattern; see the attached figure.

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - all four options are drawn magnetic field-line patterns labelled (a) to (d); the options ARE the figure, and describing them would state the answer, so the placeholders below withhold the shapes. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
Inside a long current-carrying solenoid the magnetic field lines are parallel straight lines, all pointing in the same direction, which shows that the field there is uniform. The diagram of equally spaced parallel straight lines with arrows in one direction shows exactly this.

(The concentric circles are the field around a straight current-carrying wire. The pattern with lines curving round from end to end shows the whole solenoid, including the field outside it, and the question asks only about the inside.)

This is option (A), the set of parallel straight field lines.

rows.stem: Identify the food chain in which the organisms of the second trophic level are missing :

options.label: B
options.text: Zooplankton, Phytoplankton, small fish, large fish

rows.solution:
A food chain begins with a producer (first trophic level), followed by a herbivore (second trophic level) and then carnivores. Arranged by who eats whom, tiger, grass, snake, frog becomes grass, frog, snake, tiger. A frog does not eat grass, so the herbivore (such as a grasshopper) that should sit between the grass and the frog is missing.

Each of the other chains has a herbivore after its producer: grass, goat, lion; phytoplankton, zooplankton, small fish, large fish; grass, grasshopper, frog, snake, eagle.

This is option (C) Tiger, grass, snake, frog.

rows.stem: In which of the following organisms, multiple fission is a means of asexual reproduction ?
rows.solution:
In multiple fission a single cell divides into many daughter cells at the same time. *Plasmodium*, the malarial parasite, reproduces in this way. (Yeast reproduces by budding, while *Leishmania* and *Paramoecium* divide by binary fission.)

This is option (D) Plasmodium.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Hydrogen gas is not evolved when zinc reacts with nitric acid.

**Reason (R) :** Nitric acid oxidises the hydrogen gas produced to water and itself gets reduced.
rows.context: For Q. Nos. 17 to 20, two statements are given – One labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Hydrogen gas is not evolved when zinc reacts with nitric acid, so the Assertion is true. This is because nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent: it oxidises the hydrogen produced to water and is itself reduced to oxides of nitrogen.

The Reason is true and explains the Assertion. This is option (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Accumulation of harmful chemicals is maximum in the organisms at the highest trophic level of a food chain.

**Reason (R) :** Harmful chemicals are sprayed on the crops to protect them from diseases and pests.
rows.context: For Q. Nos. 17 to 20, two statements are given – One labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Harmful chemicals such as pesticides are not degradable. They enter the food chain and accumulate progressively at each trophic level (biological magnification), so their concentration is maximum in organisms at the highest trophic level. The Assertion is true.

Such chemicals are indeed sprayed on crops to protect them from diseases and pests, so the Reason is true. But the spraying only explains how the chemicals enter the food chain; it does not explain why they build up at the top, which happens because they are non-biodegradable.

Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The rate of breathing in aquatic organisms is much faster than in terrestrial organisms.

**Reason (R) :** The amount of oxygen dissolved in water is very high as compared to the amount of oxygen in air.
rows.context: For Q. Nos. 17 to 20, two statements are given – One labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Aquatic organisms breathe much faster than terrestrial organisms, so the Assertion is true. They need to, because the amount of oxygen dissolved in water is very low compared with the amount of oxygen in air. The Reason says the opposite, so the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The rainbow is a natural spectrum of sunlight in the sky.

**Reason (R) :** Rainbow is formed in the sky when the sun is overhead and water droplets are also present in air.
rows.context: For Q. Nos. 17 to 20, two statements are given – One labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
A rainbow is a natural spectrum of sunlight appearing in the sky after a rain shower, so the Assertion is true. A rainbow is always formed in the direction opposite to the sun: it is seen when the sun is behind the observer and low in the sky, not when the sun is overhead. So the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem: Name the type of chemical reaction in which calcium oxide reacts with water. Justify your answer by giving balanced chemical equation for the chemical reaction.
rows.solution:
Calcium oxide (quicklime) reacts vigorously with water to form slaked lime (calcium hydroxide), and a large amount of heat is released:

\(\mathrm{CaO(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2(aq)}\) + heat

Two substances combine to form a single product, so it is a combination reaction. (Since heat is given out, it is also an exothermic reaction.)

rows.stem:
State one role of each of the following in human digestive system :

(i) Hydrochloric acid

(ii) Villi

(iii) Anal Sphincter

(iv) Lipase
rows.solution:
(i) Hydrochloric acid creates an acidic medium in the stomach, which helps the enzyme pepsin act; it also kills germs that enter with the food.

(ii) Villi, the finger-like projections of the inner lining of the small intestine, increase the surface area for the absorption of digested food.

(iii) The anal sphincter regulates the exit of the waste material (undigested food) through the anus.

(iv) Lipase breaks down (digests) the emulsified fats into fatty acids and glycerol.

rows.stem: How is the movement of leaves of a sensitive plant different from the downward movement of the roots ?
rows.solution:
Any two differences:

| Movement of leaves of a sensitive plant | Downward movement of roots |
|---|---|
| The stimulus is touch | The stimulus is gravity |
| No growth is involved; the leaf cells change shape by changing the amount of water in them | Growth is involved; the root bends as it grows |
| Non-directional: the movement does not depend on the direction of the stimulus | Directional: the root grows towards the pull of gravity (positive geotropism) |

rows.stem: There is a hormone which regulates carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism in our body. Name the hormone and the gland which secretes it. Why is it important for us to have iodised salt in our diet?
rows.solution:
The hormone is thyroxine, and it is secreted by the thyroid gland.

Iodine is necessary for the thyroid gland to make thyroxine. If our diet is short of iodine, too little thyroxine is made and we may suffer from goitre, in which the neck appears swollen. Iodised salt makes sure that we get enough iodine.

rows.stem: An object is placed at a distance of 10 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position of the image formed by the mirror.
rows.solution:
For a convex mirror, \(u = -10\) cm and \(f = +15\) cm. By the mirror formula,

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{2 + 3}{30} = \dfrac{1}{6}\), so \(v = +6\) cm.

The image is formed 6 cm behind the mirror; it is virtual and erect.

rows.stem: Show how you would connect three resistors each of resistance \(6\,\Omega\), so that the combination has a resistance of \(9\,\Omega\). Also justify your answer.
rows.solution:
Connect two of the \(6\,\Omega\) resistors in parallel, and connect the third \(6\,\Omega\) resistor in series with this pair.

Justification: the parallel pair has resistance given by \(\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{2}{6}\), so \(R_p = 3\,\Omega\). Adding the third resistor in series gives \(R = 6 + 3 = 9\,\Omega\).

(The marking scheme gives the mark for the arrangement either stated in words or shown in a circuit diagram.)

rows.stem: In the given circuit calculate the power consumed in watts in the resistor of \(2\,\Omega\) :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit (a 1 Ω and a 2 Ω resistor in series with a 6 V battery and a plug key) is given only as a drawing; the resistor values and the EMF appear nowhere else. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
The \(1\,\Omega\) and \(2\,\Omega\) resistors are in series with the 6 V battery (with the key closed), so the total resistance is

\(R = 1 + 2 = 3\,\Omega\).

The current in the circuit is \(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2\) A, and the same current flows through both resistors.

Power consumed in the \(2\,\Omega\) resistor: \(P = I^2 R = (2)^2 \times 2 = 8\) W.

rows.stem:
(i) Two magnetic field lines do not intersect each other. Why ?

(ii) How is a uniform magnetic field in a given region represented ? Draw a diagram in support of your answer.
rows.solution:
(i) If two field lines intersected, then at the point of intersection the magnetic field would have two directions, and a compass needle placed there would have to point in two directions at once, which is not possible.

(ii) A uniform magnetic field is represented by equally spaced (equidistant) parallel straight lines, all with arrows pointing in the same direction.

Diagram: draw four or five parallel straight lines at equal spacing, each with an arrowhead pointing the same way. (The field inside a long current-carrying solenoid is an example.)

rows.stem:
Write one chemical equation each for the chemical reaction in which the following have taken place :

(i) Change in colour

(ii) Change in temperature

(iii) Formation of precipitate

Mention colour change/temperature change (rise/fall)/compound precipitated along with equation.
rows.solution:
(i) Change in colour: an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turns the blue solution green, because iron displaces copper.

\(\mathrm{Fe(s) + CuSO_4(aq) \rightarrow FeSO_4(aq) + Cu(s)}\)

(blue solution \(\rightarrow\) green solution)

(ii) Change in temperature: when an acid neutralises a base, heat is given out and the temperature rises.

\(\mathrm{NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) \rightarrow NaCl(aq) + H_2O(l)}\) + heat

(iii) Formation of precipitate: lead nitrate and potassium iodide solutions react to give a yellow precipitate of lead iodide, \(\mathrm{PbI_2}\).

\(\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2(aq) + 2KI(aq) \rightarrow PbI_2(s) + 2KNO_3(aq)}\)

(Any other reaction showing each change is equally acceptable.)

rows.stem:
(i) The pH of a sample of tomato juice is 4.6. How is this juice likely to be in taste ? Give reason to justify your answer.

(ii) How do we differentiate between a strong acid and a weak base in terms of ion-formation in aqueous solutions ?

(iii) The acid rain can make the survival of aquatic animals difficult. How ?
rows.solution:
(i) The juice will taste sour. A pH of 4.6 is below 7, so the juice is acidic, and acids taste sour.

(ii) A strong acid ionises almost completely in water and gives a large number of \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions (\(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\) ions). A weak base ionises only partly and gives a small number of \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) ions.

(iii) Aquatic animals can survive only in a narrow range of pH, close to 7 (about 7.0 to 7.8). Acid rain has a pH below 5.6; when it flows into rivers and lakes it lowers the pH of the water below this range, which makes the survival of aquatic animals difficult.

rows.stem:
(i) Why is respiratory pigment needed in multicellular organisms with large body size ?

(ii) Give reasons for the following :

(a) Rings of cartilage are present in the throat.

(b) Lungs always contain a residual volume of air.

(c) The diaphragm flattens and ribs are lifted up when we breathe in.

(d) Walls of alveoli contain an extensive network of blood vessels.
rows.solution:
(i) In a large multicellular organism, diffusion alone cannot supply oxygen fast enough to all parts of the body, because the distances are too great. A respiratory pigment (haemoglobin in human beings) takes up oxygen in the lungs and carries it in the blood to the tissues.

(ii) (a) The rings of cartilage keep the air passage (the trachea) open, so that it does not collapse.

(b) The residual volume of air ensures that there is sufficient time for oxygen to be absorbed and for carbon dioxide to be released.

(c) When the diaphragm flattens and the ribs are lifted, the chest cavity becomes larger, so air is sucked into the lungs.

(d) Exchange of gases takes place in the alveoli. The network of blood vessels in their walls lets oxygen pass into the blood and carbon dioxide pass out of it.

rows.stem: Define reflex action. With the help of a flow chart show the path of a reflex action such as sneezing.
rows.solution:
A reflex action is a sudden, automatic (involuntary) response to a stimulus in the environment, made without thinking. Sneezing is an example.

Path of a reflex action such as sneezing:

Stimulus (irritant in the nose) \(\rightarrow\) receptors (in the nose) \(\rightarrow\) sensory neuron \(\rightarrow\) relay neuron in the spinal cord \(\rightarrow\) motor neuron \(\rightarrow\) effector (muscles) \(\rightarrow\) response (sneezing)

The marking scheme's chart is this general reflex arc through the spinal cord. For sneezing in particular, the relay centre lies in the medulla of the hind-brain, which continues into the spinal cord; any other example of a reflex action is also accepted.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem:
Study the diagram given below and answer the questions that follow :

(i) Name the defect of vision represented in the diagram. Give reason for your answer.

(ii) List two causes of this defect.

(iii) With the help of a diagram show how this defect of vision is corrected.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the defect exists only in the drawing: an eye with two points N and N′ marked on the axis in front of it and rays from N′ passing through the eye lens; where those rays meet relative to the retina is the quantity under test and is withheld here. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
(i) The defect is hypermetropia (far-sightedness). In the diagram, rays from the point \(N'\), the near point of a normal eye, come to a focus behind the retina, so the eye cannot see a nearby object clearly. The near point of this eye has moved farther away, to N, beyond the normal 25 cm.

(ii) The two causes are: the focal length of the eye lens is too long, and the eyeball has become too small.

(iii) The defect is corrected with a convex (converging) lens of suitable power.

Diagram: draw the eye with a convex lens placed in front of it. Rays from an object at \(N'\) are bent by the convex lens so that they appear to come from N, the near point of the defective eye; the eye lens then brings them to a focus on the retina. Mark N (near point of the hypermetropic eye), \(N'\) (near point of a normal eye) and the convex lens, with arrows on the rays.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem:
Name and state the rule to determine the direction of a :

(i) magnetic field produced around a current carrying straight conductor.

(ii) force experienced by a current carrying straight conductor placed in a magnetic field which is perpendicular to it.
rows.solution:
(i) Right-hand thumb rule: imagine holding the current-carrying straight conductor in your right hand so that the thumb points in the direction of the current. Then the fingers wrapped around the conductor give the direction of the field lines of the magnetic field.

(ii) Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of your left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb points in the direction of the motion of, or the force acting on, the conductor.

rows.stem:
Plants \(\rightarrow\) Deer \(\rightarrow\) Lion

In the given food chain, what will be the impact of removing all the organisms of second trophic level on the first and third trophic level? Will the impact be the same for the organisms of the third trophic level in the above food chain if they were present in a food web? Justify.
rows.solution:
If all the deer (the second trophic level) are removed, the plants (first trophic level) are no longer eaten, so their number will increase. The lions (third trophic level) lose their only food, so their number will decrease and they may starve to death.

No, the impact would not be the same in a food web. In a food web each organism has several sources of food, so the lions would find other prey and would not starve. A food web is therefore more stable than a single food chain.

rows.stem:
A gas ‘X’ which is a deadly poison is found at the higher levels of atmosphere and performs an essential function.

Name the gas and write the function performed by this gas in the atmosphere. Which chemical is linked to the decrease in the level of this gas? What measures have been taken by an international organization to check the depletion of the layer containing this gas?
rows.solution:
The gas X is ozone, \(\mathrm{O_3}\).

Ozone in the upper atmosphere shields the surface of the earth from the harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation of the sun.

The decrease in the amount of ozone is linked to chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers.

In 1987 the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) succeeded in forging an agreement to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels. It has also become mandatory for manufacturing companies to make CFC-free refrigerators.

rows.stem:
(i) Define a homologous series of carbon compounds.

(ii) Why is the melting and boiling points of \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\) higher than that of \(\mathrm{C_3H_6}\) or \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\) ?

(iii) Why do we **NOT** see any gradation in chemical properties of a homologous series compounds ?

(iv) Write the name and structures of (i) aldehyde and (ii) ketone with molecular form \(\mathrm{C_3H_6O}\).
rows.solution:
(i) A homologous series is a series of carbon compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in a carbon chain. Its members have the same general formula and similar chemical properties, and successive members differ by a \(\mathrm{CH_2}\) unit.

(ii) Melting and boiling points increase with increasing molecular mass. \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\) (molecular mass 56 u) is heavier than \(\mathrm{C_3H_6}\) (42 u) and \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\) (28 u), so its melting and boiling points are higher.

(iii) The chemical properties of a carbon compound are determined by its functional group. All members of a homologous series have the same functional group, so their chemical properties are similar and show no gradation.

(iv) (I) The aldehyde is propanal, \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}\). Structure: a \(\mathrm{CH_3}\) group joined to a \(\mathrm{CH_2}\) group, which is joined to a carbon carrying a double-bonded oxygen and a hydrogen (the \(\mathrm{-CHO}\) group at the end of the chain).

(II) The ketone is propanone (acetone), \(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\). Structure: a central carbon carrying a double-bonded oxygen, joined on each side to a \(\mathrm{CH_3}\) group.

rows.stem:
(i) Write the name and structure of an organic compound ‘X’ having two carbon atoms in its molecule and its name is suffixed with ‘–ol’.

(ii) What happens when ‘X’ is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K? Write chemical equation for the reaction stating the conditions for the reaction. Also state the role played by concentrated sulphuric acid in the reaction.

(iii) Name and draw the electron dot structure of hydrocarbon produced in the above reaction.
rows.solution:
(i) X is ethanol, \(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}\) (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}\)). Structure: two carbon atoms joined by a single bond; the first carbon carries three hydrogen atoms, and the second carries two hydrogen atoms and an \(\mathrm{-OH}\) group.

(ii) When ethanol is heated at 443 K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid, it loses a molecule of water and forms ethene:

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{hot conc. } H_2SO_4,\ 443\,K} CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2O}\)

The conditions (concentrated sulphuric acid, 443 K) must be written in the equation: the marking scheme deducts half a mark if they are left out. Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent, removing water from ethanol.

(iii) The hydrocarbon is ethene, \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\). Electron dot structure: the two carbon atoms share two pairs of electrons with each other (a double bond), and each carbon shares one pair of electrons with each of two hydrogen atoms. Each carbon then has eight electrons in its outer shell and each hydrogen has two (\(\mathrm{H_2C{=}CH_2}\) in structural form).

rows.stem:
(i) Name three techniques/devices used by human females to avoid pregnancy. Mention the side effects caused by each.

(ii) What will happen if in a human female (a) fertilisation takes place, (b) an egg is not fertilised ?
rows.solution:
(i) Any three techniques, with their side effects:

1. Oral pills (a chemical method): they change the hormonal balance of the body, which can cause side effects.

2. A loop or copper-T placed in the uterus: it can cause irritation of the uterus.

3. Surgical method, blocking the fallopian tubes: if not performed properly it can cause infection and other problems.

(ii) (a) If fertilisation takes place, the fertilised egg (zygote) gets implanted in the thick, blood-rich lining of the uterus and starts dividing to form an embryo. The placenta develops and supplies the embryo with nourishment from the mother's blood.

(b) If the egg is not fertilised, the thick and spongy lining of the uterus is not needed. It slowly breaks down and comes out through the vagina as blood and mucus (menstruation).

rows.stem:
(i) Draw a diagram showing spore formation in Rhizopus and label the (a) reproductive and (b) non-reproductive parts. Why does Rhizopus not multiply on a dry slice of bread ?

(ii) Name and explain the process by which reproduction takes place in Hydra.
rows.solution:
(i) Diagram of spore formation in *Rhizopus*: draw a network of thread-like hyphae on the bread, with several upright stalks rising from it, each ending in a round knob (a sporangium) containing spores, and show spores being released from one of them. Label:

(a) reproductive part: sporangia (containing the spores);

(b) non-reproductive part: hyphae.

*Rhizopus* does not multiply on a dry slice of bread because the dry bread does not provide the moisture (and nutrients) that the spores need to germinate and grow.

(ii) *Hydra* reproduces by budding. *Hydra* uses its regenerative cells for reproduction: a bud develops as an outgrowth because of repeated cell division at one specific site. The bud grows into a tiny individual, and when mature it detaches from the parent and becomes a new independent individual.

(Regeneration is also accepted: if *Hydra* is cut into many pieces, many of the pieces grow into separate individuals, through specialised cells.)

rows.stem:
(i) Define electric power. Express it in terms of potential difference (V) and resistance (R).

(ii) An electric oven is designed to work on the mains voltage of 220 V. This oven consumes 11 units of electrical energy in 5 hours. Calculate :

(a) power rating of the oven

(b) current drawn by the oven

(c) resistance of the oven when it is red hot
rows.solution:
(i) Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed (dissipated) in a circuit.

\(P = VI\), and with \(I = \dfrac{V}{R}\) this gives \(P = \dfrac{V^2}{R}\).

(ii) (a) 1 unit = 1 kWh, so the oven consumes 11 kWh in 5 h.

\(P = \dfrac{\text{energy consumed}}{\text{time}} = \dfrac{11\ \text{kWh}}{5\ \text{h}} = 2.2\) kW \(= 2200\) W.

(b) \(I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{2200}{220} = 10\) A.

(c) \(R = \dfrac{V^2}{P} = \dfrac{(220)^2}{2200} = \dfrac{48400}{2200} = 22\,\Omega\). (Equally, \(R = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{220}{10} = 22\,\Omega\).)

rows.stem:
(i) Write the relation between resistance R and electrical resistivity \(\rho\) of the material of a conductor in the shape of cylinder of length *l* and area of cross-section A. Hence derive the SI unit of electrical resistivity.

(ii) The resistance of a metal wire of length 3 m is \(60\,\Omega\). If the area of cross-section of the wire is \(4 \times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{m^2}\), calculate the electrical resistivity of the wire.

(iii) State how would electrical resistivity be affected if the wire (of part ‘ii’) is stretched so that its length is doubled. Justify your answer.
rows.solution:
(i) \(R = \rho \dfrac{l}{A}\), so \(\rho = \dfrac{RA}{l}\).

SI unit of \(\rho\): \(\dfrac{\Omega \times \mathrm{m^2}}{\mathrm{m}} = \Omega\,\mathrm{m}\) (ohm metre).

(ii) Here \(l = 3\) m, \(A = 4 \times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{m^2}\) and \(R = 60\,\Omega\).

\(\rho = \dfrac{RA}{l} = \dfrac{60 \times 4 \times 10^{-7}}{3} = 80 \times 10^{-7}\,\Omega\,\mathrm{m} = 8 \times 10^{-6}\,\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\).

(iii) The resistivity will not change. Resistivity does not depend on the length or the area of cross-section of the conductor; it depends only on the nature of its material (at a given temperature). Stretching changes the resistance of the wire, but not its resistivity.

rows.stem: What is the cathode and anode made of in the refining of copper by this process ?
rows.context: The metals produced by various reduction processes are not very pure. They contain impurities, which must be removed to obtain pure metals. The most widely used method for refining impure metals is electrolytic refining.
rows.solution: In the electrolytic refining of copper, the cathode is a thin strip of pure copper and the anode is the impure copper.

rows.stem: Name the solution used in the above process and write its formula.
rows.context: The metals produced by various reduction processes are not very pure. They contain impurities, which must be removed to obtain pure metals. The most widely used method for refining impure metals is electrolytic refining.
rows.solution: The electrolyte is a solution of acidified copper sulphate, \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\) (copper sulphate solution with a little dilute sulphuric acid).

rows.stem: How copper gets refined when electric current is passed in the electrolytic cell ?
rows.context: The metals produced by various reduction processes are not very pure. They contain impurities, which must be removed to obtain pure metals. The most widely used method for refining impure metals is electrolytic refining.
rows.solution:
[CBSE marking scheme: says "pure copper from the anode dissolves into electrolyte"; the anode is the impure copper (as its own answer to part (i) states), so it is the impure copper of the anode that dissolves.]

When current is passed, the impure copper from the anode dissolves into the electrolyte as copper ions, and an equivalent amount of pure copper from the electrolyte is deposited on the cathode:

At the anode: \(\mathrm{Cu \rightarrow Cu^{2+} + 2e^-}\)

At the cathode: \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Cu}\) (pure)

The soluble impurities go into the solution, while the insoluble impurities settle down at the bottom of the anode as anode mud. (Explaining the process with a suitable labelled diagram also earns the marks.)

rows.stem: You have two beakers ‘A’ and ‘B’ containing copper sulphate solution. What would you observe after about 2 hours if you dip a strip of zinc in beaker ‘A’ and a strip of silver in beaker ‘B’? Give reason for your observations in each case.
rows.context: The metals produced by various reduction processes are not very pure. They contain impurities, which must be removed to obtain pure metals. The most widely used method for refining impure metals is electrolytic refining.
rows.solution:
Beaker A (zinc strip): the blue colour of the solution fades and it becomes colourless, and a reddish-brown coating of copper forms on the zinc strip. Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulphate:

\(\mathrm{Zn(s) + CuSO_4(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_4(aq) + Cu(s)}\)

Beaker B (silver strip): no change is seen and the solution stays blue. Silver is less reactive than copper, so it cannot displace copper from copper sulphate.

rows.stem: When Mendel crossed pea plants with pure tall and pure short characteristics to produce \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny, which two observations were made by him in \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants?
rows.context: Mendel worked out the rules of heredity by working on garden pea using a number of visible contrasting characters. He conducted several experiments by making a cross with one or two pairs of contrasting characters of pea plant. On the basis of his observations he gave some interpretations which helped to study the mechanism of inheritance.
rows.solution: In the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation all the plants were tall; no short plants were seen. No plants of medium height appeared either: only the dominant parental trait was seen, not a mixture of the two.

rows.stem: Write one difference between dominant and recessive trait.
rows.context: Mendel worked out the rules of heredity by working on garden pea using a number of visible contrasting characters. He conducted several experiments by making a cross with one or two pairs of contrasting characters of pea plant. On the basis of his observations he gave some interpretations which helped to study the mechanism of inheritance.
rows.solution: A dominant trait is expressed even when only a single copy of it is present, while a recessive trait is expressed only when it is present in a pair (two copies).

rows.stem:
In a cross with two pairs of contrasting characters

RRYY \(\times\) rryy

(Round Yellow) (Wrinkled Green)

Mendel observed 4 types of combinations in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation. By which method did he obtain \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation ? Write the ratio of the parental combinations obtained and what conclusions were drawn from this experiment.
rows.context: Mendel worked out the rules of heredity by working on garden pea using a number of visible contrasting characters. He conducted several experiments by making a cross with one or two pairs of contrasting characters of pea plant. On the basis of his observations he gave some interpretations which helped to study the mechanism of inheritance.
rows.solution:
Mendel obtained the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation by self-pollination of the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants (all RrYy, round and yellow).

In the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation the four combinations appear in the ratio round yellow : round green : wrinkled yellow : wrinkled green \(= 9 : 3 : 3 : 1\). The parental combinations are round yellow and wrinkled green, so they are obtained in the ratio round yellow : wrinkled green \(= 9 : 1\).

Conclusion: new combinations (round green and wrinkled yellow) also appeared, so the traits for seed shape and seed colour are inherited independently of each other.

rows.stem:
Justify the statement :

“It is possible that a trait is inherited but may not be expressed.”
rows.context: Mendel worked out the rules of heredity by working on garden pea using a number of visible contrasting characters. He conducted several experiments by making a cross with one or two pairs of contrasting characters of pea plant. On the basis of his observations he gave some interpretations which helped to study the mechanism of inheritance.
rows.solution:
When pea plants with yellow seeds are crossed with plants with green seeds, all the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants have yellow seeds. When the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are self-pollinated, the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation has plants with yellow seeds and plants with green seeds.

The green-seed trait reappears in \(\mathrm{F_2}\), so the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants must have inherited it, even though it was not seen in them. Both traits were inherited, but only one (the dominant trait) was expressed in the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny while the other remained unexpressed. So a trait can be inherited but not expressed. (The same can be shown with any one characteristic, such as tall and short plants, or with a diagram.)

rows.stem: In which one of the above cases the mirror will form a diminished image of the object ? Justify your answer.
rows.context:
Study the data given below showing the focal length of three concave mirrors A, B and C and the respective distances of objects placed in front of the mirrors :

| Case | Mirror | Focal Length (cm) | Object Distance (cm) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A | 20 | 45 |
| 2 | B | 15 | 30 |
| 3 | C | 30 | 20 |
rows.solution: Case 1, mirror A. Its focal length is 20 cm, so its centre of curvature is at 40 cm. The object at 45 cm is beyond the centre of curvature, so the image is formed between F and C and is diminished (real and inverted).

rows.stem: List two properties of the image formed in case 2.
rows.context:
Study the data given below showing the focal length of three concave mirrors A, B and C and the respective distances of objects placed in front of the mirrors :

| Case | Mirror | Focal Length (cm) | Object Distance (cm) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A | 20 | 45 |
| 2 | B | 15 | 30 |
| 3 | C | 30 | 20 |
rows.solution: In case 2 the object is at 30 cm, which is the centre of curvature of mirror B (focal length 15 cm), so the image is also formed at C. Any two properties: it is real, inverted and of the same size as the object.

rows.stem: What is the nature and size of the image formed by mirror C ? Draw ray diagram to justify your answer.
rows.context:
Study the data given below showing the focal length of three concave mirrors A, B and C and the respective distances of objects placed in front of the mirrors :

| Case | Mirror | Focal Length (cm) | Object Distance (cm) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A | 20 | 45 |
| 2 | B | 15 | 30 |
| 3 | C | 30 | 20 |
rows.solution:
For mirror C the focal length is 30 cm and the object is at 20 cm, between the pole and the focus. The image is virtual and erect (nature), and magnified (size), formed behind the mirror.

Ray diagram: draw the concave mirror with its pole P, focus F and centre of curvature C on the principal axis, and the object AB between P and F. From A draw a ray parallel to the principal axis; after reflection it passes through F. From A draw a second ray along the line from C through A; it falls normally on the mirror and is reflected back along itself. The two reflected rays diverge; produce them backwards (dotted) behind the mirror, where they meet at \(A'\). Drop a perpendicular \(A'B'\) to the axis: the image \(A'B'\) is virtual, erect and larger than AB. Draw arrows on the rays: the marking scheme deducts half a mark if they are missing.

rows.stem: An object is placed at a distance of 18 cm from the pole of a concave mirror of focal length 12 cm. Find the position of the image formed in this case.
rows.context:
Study the data given below showing the focal length of three concave mirrors A, B and C and the respective distances of objects placed in front of the mirrors :

| Case | Mirror | Focal Length (cm) | Object Distance (cm) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A | 20 | 45 |
| 2 | B | 15 | 30 |
| 3 | C | 30 | 20 |
rows.solution:
For a concave mirror, \(f = -12\) cm and \(u = -18\) cm. By the mirror formula,

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{1}{18} = \dfrac{-3 + 2}{36} = -\dfrac{1}{36}\), so \(v = -36\) cm.

The image is formed in front of the mirror, 36 cm from its pole. (The object is between F and C, so the image is real, inverted and magnified.)
